subject: DPA & SCCs redline consolidation — evidence and fallback options
messages:
From: Emma White <emma.white@novasys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Novasys Legal <legal@novasys.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novasys DPA redlines + hosting/sccs questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team appreciated the performance numbers. Attached is our legal team's updated DPA (Novasys_DPA_redline_v2.docx). There are a few substantive asks we need to resolve before we can sign the MSA+Order Form: 

- SCCs fallback language: we need clarity on which alternate SCCs we'd fall back to if the EU Commission list changes.
- Controller/Processor role map: the redline switches some responsibilities from Processor to Controller for derivative analytics; can you confirm Redwood's stance?
- Transfer impact addendum: since we will store personal data in EU and US regions, they want an explicit transfer-impact addendum and a short plan for mitigations (encryption at rest, KMS, region pinning).
- Evidence: they asked for the latest SOC 2 scope and a copy of the pen-test summary.

We'd like to get legal sign-off this month — can Redwood provide a consolidated markup and a recommended fallback clause (2 options: conservative + commercially reasonable)?

Thanks,
Emma
Legal Ops — Novasys Inc.
Attachment: Novasys_DPA_redline_v2.docx (document)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma White <emma.white@novasys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novasys DPA redlines + hosting/sccs questions

Emma — thanks for sending. Looping in Ben (contracts) and Laura (legal ops / evidence) to own the redline + controls delivery. High-level plan from Redwood: 

1) Ben will produce a single consolidated DPA response that shows: accepted language, proposed compromise redlines, and two fallback SCCs approaches ("SCC-first" conservative, and "risk-mapped" commercially reasonable).
2) Laura will share SOC 2 scope and a redacted pen-test executive summary.
3) We'll return a tracked document and a short cover memo explaining operational mitigations and how the order form's hosting pins will be enforced.

Can you confirm the Novasys preferred signoff deadline? We'll aim to send our consolidated response by 2026-08-17 EOD PT, but if you need faster we can prioritize the SCC fallback options first.

— Soojin
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

On Aug 14, 2026, at 09:12 AM, Emma White <emma.white@novasys.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Novasys DPA redlines + hosting/sccs questions

Team — draft approach and talking points below. I'll turn this into a tracked-response doc and a short cover memo for Emma.

Key points to include in our consolidated response:
- SCCs fallback: propose a two-tier clause. Tier 1 (preferred): reference the current EU Commission SCCs (2021 modules) with a defined mapping to vendor responsibilities; include an automatic "substitution by Commission" mechanism plus a 90-day operational remediation window. Tier 2 (fallback): if a new adequacy regime removes the SCCs we will rely on: (a) adopt the Commission's new standard SCCs, or (b) if unavailable, rely on documented ADP/technical safeguards (encryption, KMS, region pinning) plus a contractual cross-border safeguard that both parties will negotiate in good faith.
- Controller/Processor: Redwood will remain Processor for the services described in the Order Form. Analytics outputs that materially re-identify individuals are explicitly out of scope unless a separate Processing Addendum is agreed — propose a short carveout sentence.
- Transfer-impact addendum: offer a 1-page addendum that enumerates transfer routes, subprocessor country list, KMS controls, data residency pinning, and audit access. This will be an exhibit to the Order Form.

Attachments to send with our response: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (redacted), redline_response_novasys_v1.docx (we'll generate).

I'll produce the tracked redline by EOD tomorrow (Aug 16) and will call out three items I expect to escalate to legal for sign-off: the 90-day remediation window, a carveout on analytics, and the proposed language for automatic substitution of SCCs.

— Ben
Principal, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_outline.txt (notes)

From: Emma White <emma.white@novasys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novasys DPA redlines + hosting/sccs questions

Thanks — that approach sounds reasonable. A couple of clarifications from Novasys Legal: 

- The 90-day remediation window is OK provided there are clear interim measures (e.g., temporary processing restrictions, logfile retention adjustments).
- On the analytics carveout: they want an explicit notification step if Redwood intends to run re-identification or model-training that uses personal data beyond simple aggregated metrics.
- For evidence: we need SOC 2 + either a short pen-test executive summary or a vulnerability remediation SLA item.

Signoff timeline: Novasys can target internal legal approval by 2026-08-20 if we have a consolidated response by Aug 17 morning ET. If you can provide the SCC fallback options as a top-line bullet earlier today that will help our counsel.

— Emma
Novasys Legal Ops

Cc: Emma White <emma.white@novasys.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidated response + evidence delivery 

Emma / team — attaching our consolidated package and quick notes.

Attachment: redline_response_novasys_v1.docx (tracked), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (redacted), pen-test-exec-summary.txt (redacted)

Cover notes (top-line):
- SCC fallback options (top-line bullets for Novasys counsel):
  1) Conservative: reference existing 2021 SCCs; automatic substitution by the Commission with a 90-day remediation period; interim technical limits during remediation.
  2) Commercially reasonable: allow substitution or equivalent safeguards (encryption + KMS + contractual cross-border clause) with a 30-day notice + joint remediation plan.
- Controller/Processor: retained as Processor; proposed carveout text added to the redline for any re-identification/model-training beyond aggregate metrics — requires separate DPA exhibit.
- Transfer-impact addendum: attached as Exhibit A; enumerates subprocessors by country and routing rules.
- Evidence: SOC 2 (redacted) and pen-test executive summary attached; we offered a vulnerability remediation SLA clause in the redline (30-day median patch timeline, priority SLA for critical exploits).

Next steps I recommend:
- Ben to follow up on the three legal escalation items and confirm final language tomorrow.
- Soojin to confirm whether Novasys needs an on-site or additional attestation for SOC 2 scope.
- Emma to confirm Novasys internal deadline (Aug 20) and whether DocuSign should be prepared for a conditional MSA signature with Exhibit A pending subprocessor additions.

Thanks all — Laura
Senior Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
